title: Hard-sphere dynamics and kinetic limits
summary: Finitely many hard spheres of diameter ε in a flat position space (Euclidean space or a flat torus): elastic scattering, trajectories, Alexander's theorem (the hard-sphere flow exists off a null set and is a measure-preserving group), its Koopman group, transported densities and the weak Liouville equation with specular reflection, marginals, Maxwellian canonical and grand canonical ensembles with their invariance and correlation functions, the hard-sphere Boltzmann collision operator and mild solutions, Lanford's theorem stated as a proposition, and its law of large numbers for the rescaled empirical measure.

targets.name: FlatPositionSpace
targets.statement: Class FlatPositionSpace d X on a proper normed additive commutative group X with Borel measurable structure and a measure volume: data an additive homomorphism π : E →+ X (E = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) and a radius ρ ∈ (0, ∞]; axioms: π surjective; ‖π a‖ ≤ |a|; every ξ with ‖ξ‖ < ρ has a lift a with π a = ξ and |a| = ‖ξ‖; π injective on B(0, ρ); volume translation invariant; volume(π(A)) = vol(A) for measurable A ⊆ B(0, ρ).

api.name: shortLift
api.statement: For ‖ξ‖ < ρ the unique ℓ(ξ) ∈ B(0, ρ) with π(ℓ ξ) = ξ; |ℓ ξ| = ‖ξ‖, ℓ(−ξ) = −ℓ ξ, ℓ(π a) = a for |a| < ρ, ℓ continuous on the ball.

api.name: norm_cover_sub
api.statement: π is 1-Lipschitz and ‖π a − π b‖ = |a − b| when |a − b| < ρ; π(B(a, r)) = B(π a, r) for r ≤ ρ.

api.name: volume_ball
api.statement: volume(B(x, r)) = vol(B(0, r)) for r ≤ ρ; spheres of radius 0 < r < ρ are null.

api.name: isAddHaarMeasure
api.statement: volume is an additive Haar measure, σ-finite, finite on bounded sets and regular.

api.name: measurePreserving_add_cover
api.statement: x ↦ x + π(t v) is a measure-preserving homeomorphism and (t, x) ↦ x + π(t v) is continuous.

tests.name: euclidean_instance

targets.name: FlatTorus
targets.statement: For L : Submodule ℤ E with DiscreteTopology L and IsZLattice ℝ L, FlatTorus L = E ⧸ L.toAddSubgroup with the quotient norm (QuotientAddGroup.instNormedAddCommGroup, L closed since discrete), the Borel σ-algebra (QuotientAddGroup.borelSpace) and the MeasureSpace instance whose volume is the image of Lebesgue measure restricted to the fundamental domain ZSpan.fundamentalDomain of a chosen ℤ-basis of L; the set is also a fundamental domain for the opposite subgroup acting by right translation (E commutative). Mathlib then gives: AddQuotientMeasureEqMeasurePreimage vol volume (MeasureTheory.IsFundamentalDomain.quotientMeasureEqMeasurePreimage_quotientMeasure, additive form), independence of the fundamental domain (MeasureTheory.IsAddFundamentalDomain.addProjection_respects_measure), measure preservation of the quotient map from vol restricted to a fundamental domain (measurePreserving_quotientAddGroup_mk_of_AddQuotientMeasureEqMeasurePreimage), and the Haar property of the finite measure volume (QuotientMeasureEqMeasurePreimage.haarMeasure_quotient, additive form). Total mass ZLattice.covolume L (ZLattice.covolume_eq_measure_fundamentalDomain). It is a FlatPositionSpace with π the quotient map and ρ half the minimal norm of a nonzero lattice vector; the local measure axiom is the unfolding of a fundamental domain over the disjoint translates of A ⊆ B(0, ρ).

api.name: isAddFundamentalDomain_op
api.statement: The chosen fundamental domain is a fundamental domain for AddSubgroup.op L.toAddSubgroup acting by right translation; volume is the image of vol restricted to every fundamental domain of L, the quotient map is measure preserving from vol restricted to any of them, and volume is a finite Haar measure (all three cited from Mathlib). Non-example: B(0, 1/2) is not a fundamental domain of ℤ^d for d ≥ 2 (its translates cover a set of density ω_d/2^d < 1).

api.name: compact_connected
api.statement: FlatTorus L is a compact connected metric group and the quotient map is a covering map and a local isometry on balls of radius ρ.

api.name: integral_periodic
api.statement: For L-periodic measurable g ≥ 0 on E, ∫ over the torus equals the integral of g over a fundamental domain.

api.name: unitTorus_equiv
api.statement: The unit torus (L = ℤᵈ) has ρ = 1/2, total mass 1, and the coordinate map is a measure-preserving additive equivalence with UnitAddTorus (Fin d); the norms differ.

api.name: scaling
api.statement: FlatTorus (c L) is isometric to FlatTorus L with distances times c and measure times c^d.

tests.statement: Unit circle (d = 1), f⁰ = ρ(x)M_{1,0}(v) with ρ(x) = 1 + 0.5 cos(2πx): the N = 1 component density (μ/Z)ρ(x)M(v) becomes (μ/Z)ρ(x − tv)M(v); at t = 1/4, x = 0, v = 1 the factor changes from 1.5 to 1, so by continuity on a positive-measure set. ρ = 1 + 1_{x=0} is nonconstant but a.e. 1 and gives the invariant measure.

targets.name: HardSphere.correlation
targets.statement: F_n(t)(Z_n) = μ^{−n} Σ_{p≥0} (1/p!) ∫ W_{n+p}(t)(Z_n, z_{n+1}, …, z_{n+p}) with W_N(t) = W⁰_N ∘ T_{−t}; E[Σ_{injective} h(z_{i_1}(t), …)] = μ^n ∫ F_n(t) h; symmetric, vanishing off 𝒟̄_n, ∫ F_n(t) = μ^{−n} E[Nat.descFactorial N n] (zero contribution from N < n); inversion formula on finite-measure X when f⁰ ≤ C₀ exp(−β₀|v|²/2) with C₀ ≥ 0, β₀ > 0, via ∫ W_{n+m}(t)(Z_n, ·) ≤ μ^{n+m} C₀^{n+m} exp(−β₀|V_n|²/2) K^m/Z with K = μ_X(X)(2π/β₀)^{d/2}.

api.name: HardSphere.lintegral_sum_distinct_eq_correlation
api.statement: E[Σ_{injective i} h(z_{i_1}(t), …, z_{i_n}(t))] = μ^n ∫ F_n(t) h for measurable h ≥ 0; real version for bounded h.

api.name: correlation_symmetric
api.statement: F_n(t) is symmetric and vanishes off 𝒟̄_n; ∫ F_n(t) = μ^{−n} E[Nat.descFactorial N n] < ∞.

api.name: correlation_inversion
api.statement: W_n(t) = μ^n Σ_p ((−μ)^p/p!) ∫ F_{n+p}(t) a.e., with absolutely convergent series, on finite-measure X when f⁰ ≤ C₀ exp(−β₀|v|²/2), C₀ ≥ 0, β₀ > 0; the series of absolute values is at most (μC₀)^n exp(−β₀|V_n|²/2) exp(2μC₀K)/Z with K = μ_X(X)(2π/β₀)^{d/2}.

tests.name: mean_number
tests.statement: n = 1, h = 1: E[N] = μ ∫ F_1(t), constant in t.

tests.name: stationary
tests.statement: For the invariant measure of §9.4, F_n(t) is independent of t.

tests.name: vacuum
tests.statement: f⁰ = 0: N = 0 a.s., F_1 = 0 = μ^{−1}E[Nat.descFactorial N 1]; the truncated quotient N!/(N − 1)! is 1 at N = 0 and would give μ^{−1}.

tests.name: descFactorial_values
tests.statement: Nat.descFactorial 1 2 = 0 (truncated 1!/(1 − 2)! = 1) and Nat.descFactorial 3 2 = 6.

targets.name: HardSphere.boltzmannGrad_scaling
targets.statement: For 0 < ε < ρ, F_n(0) = (f⁰)^{⊗n} 1_{𝒟̄_n} p_ε(X_n) with p_ε the probability of no particle within distance < ε of x_1, …, x_n; 0 ≤ (f⁰)^{⊗n}1 − F_n(0) ≤ n μ ω_d ε^d ‖ρ⁰‖_∞ (f⁰)^{⊗n}1; with μ_ε = ε^{−(d−1)} and ∫ f⁰ = 1, 1 − ω_d ε ‖ρ⁰‖_∞ ≤ ε^{d−1} E[N] ≤ 1.

tests.name: diagonal
tests.statement: Unit torus, f⁰ = M_{1,0}: at x_1 = x_2, F_2(0) = 0 < M(v_1)M(v_2) for every ε > 0, so convergence holds only off the diagonal; for a velocity density of compact support, outside the support both sides are 0.

targets.name: HardSphere.empirical
targets.statement: π_t(h)(N, Z) = μ^{−1} Σ_{i<N} h((T_t Z)_i) and π_t = μ^{−1} Σ_i δ_{(T_t Z)_i}; E[π_t(h)] = ∫ F_1(t) h and E[π_t(h)²] = μ^{−1}∫ F_1(t) h² + ∫ F_2(t) h ⊗ h.

api.name: empirical_eq
api.statement: For N ≥ 1, π_t = (N/μ) · empiricalMeasureOfFintype of the particles at time t.

tests.name: compat_value
tests.statement: N ≥ 1: π_t = (N/μ) empiricalMeasureOfFintype.

tests.name: total_mass
tests.statement: h = 1: π_t(1) = N/μ and E[π_t(1)] = E[N]/μ.

tests.name: empty
tests.statement: The empty configuration gives the zero measure, outside the range of empiricalMeasureOfFintype.

targets.name: HardSphere.collisionOperator
targets.statement: Q(g, g)(x, v) = ∫_E ∫_{S^{d−1}} ⟨w − v, ω⟩_+ (g(x, v')g(x, w') − g(x, v)g(x, w)) dσ_S(ω) dw, (v', w') = σ_ω(v, w); for measurable g with |g(x, v)| ≤ C exp(−β|v|²/2), C ≥ 0, β > 0, absolutely convergent with |Q(g, g)| ≤ C'(1 + |v|)exp(−β|v|²/2); gain/loss split; weak form for measurable ψ of polynomial growth; ∫ Q(g,g)ψ = 0 for collision invariants; Q(M, M) = 0.

api.name: loss_term
api.statement: The loss term is g(x, v) ω_{d−1} ∫ |w − v| g(x, w) dw.

api.name: weak_form
api.statement: ∫ Q(g,g)ψ = ¼∫∫∫ ⟨w − v, ω⟩_+ (g'g'_* − gg_*)(ψ + ψ_* − ψ' − ψ'_*) for measurable ψ of polynomial growth.

api.name: collision_invariants
api.statement: ∫ Q(g, g) ψ dv = 0 for ψ ∈ span{1, v_1, …, v_d, |v|²}.

tests.name: loss_value
tests.statement: Loss term at g = M_{1,0}, d = 3, v = 0: M(0) π √(8/π).

tests.name: kernel_sign
tests.statement: The kernels ⟨w − v, ω⟩_+ and ⟨v − w, ω⟩_+ give the same Q by ω ↦ −ω.

tests.name: beta_zero
tests.statement: d = 2, β = 0, C = 1, g = 1_{|v| ≥ 1}, v = 0: for w = r e_1, ω = (1,1)/√2, r > √2 both outgoing speeds are r/√2 ≥ 1 and the gain integrand is r/√2 on an open cone, so the integral diverges.

targets.name: HardSphere.IsMildBoltzmannSolution
targets.statement: For T ≥ 0, measurable f⁰ and jointly measurable f : ℝ → X × E → ℝ: there are C, β > 0 with |f(t, x, v)| ≤ C exp(−β|v|²/2) for t ∈ [0, T], and f(t, x + π(tv), v) = f⁰(x, v) + ∫_0^t Q(f(s), f(s))(x + π(sv), v) ds for t ∈ [0, T] and a.e. (x, v).

api.name: initial_value
api.statement: f(0, x, v) = f⁰(x, v) for a.e. (x, v); f⁰ inherits the Gaussian bound a.e.

api.name: restrict
api.statement: A mild solution on [0, T] is one on [0, S] for every 0 ≤ S ≤ T, with the same C, β.

api.name: characteristics
api.statement: Equivalently f(t, y, v) = f⁰(y − π(tv), v) + ∫_0^t Q(f(s), f(s))(y − π((t − s)v), v) ds for a.e. (y, v), since x ↦ x + π(tv) preserves μ_X.

tests.name: maxwellian_solution
tests.statement: f(t) = M_{β,u} is a mild solution on every [0, T].

tests.name: free_case
tests.statement: With Q replaced by 0 the solution is f⁰(x − π(tv), v); in d = 1, σ_ω(v, w) = (w, v) for ω = ±1, so Q ≡ 0 and mild solutions are a.e. the free transports.

tests.name: wrong_direction_cosine
tests.statement: Unit circle, f⁰ = (1 + 0.5cos(2πx))M_{1,0}(v): the wrongly signed f⁰(x + π(tv), v) gives 0.5M(1) along the characteristic at x = 0, v = 1, t = 1/4, where 1.5M(1) is required (and differs on a neighbourhood); spatially constant data do not discriminate.

targets.name: HardSphere.LanfordStatement
targets.statement: Proposition on 𝕋^d, d ≥ 2: ∀ C₀ ≥ 1, β₀ > 0, ∃ T₀ > 0, ∀ continuous probability density f⁰ with f⁰ ≤ C₀ e^{−β₀|v|²/2} and |f⁰(x,v) − f⁰(y,v)| ≤ C₀‖x − y‖e^{−β₀|v|²/2}, ∃ mild solution f on [0, T₀] with datum f⁰ such that, with μ_ε = ε^{−(d−1)}, for all t ∈ [0, T₀]: ∫ F^ε_n(t) g → ∫ f(t)^{⊗n} g for bounded continuous g; F^{ε_k}_n(t) → f(t)^{⊗n} a.e. along every sequence ε_k → 0⁺; ess sup_K |F^ε_1(t) − f(t)| → 0 for compact K.

locator.where: Theorem 1, lines 316–321; GST2013 Theorem 4 and Remark 3.1.1 lines 668–696, Theorem 8 lines 2069–2080; Lanford1975

api.name: lanfordStatement_zero
api.statement: At t = 0 every conclusion holds by §9.6.

api.name: lanfordStatement_lln
api.statement: The proposition implies the law of large numbers of §10.5.

tests.name: quantifiers
tests.statement: T₀ depends only on d, C₀, β₀.

tests.name: maxwellian_datum
tests.statement: For f⁰ = M_{β₀,0} admissible (C₀ ≥ (β₀/2π)^{d/2}) the solution is f(t) = f⁰ and every conclusion holds by §9.4–9.6.

tests.name: filter_vs_sequence
tests.statement: An a.e. conclusion along the filter ε → 0⁺ would depend on representatives of uncountably many functions; sequences are used.

targets.name: HardSphere.tendsto_empirical_of_correlation
targets.statement: On a flat position space with f⁰ ≥ 0 integrable, t ∈ ℝ, μ_ε → ∞ as ε → 0⁺ and f integrable: if ∫ F^ε_1(t) g → ∫ f g and ∫ F^ε_2(t) g₂ → ∫ f ⊗ f g₂ for all bounded continuous g, g₂, then P_ε(|π^ε_t(h) − ∫ f h| ≥ δ) → 0 for all bounded continuous h and δ > 0; corollary HardSphere.LanfordStatement.tendsto_empirical for d ≥ 2 under HardSphere.LanfordStatement d.

api.name: HardSphere.LanfordStatement.tendsto_empirical
api.statement: For d ≥ 2 (so μ_ε = ε^{−(d−1)} → ∞) and under HardSphere.LanfordStatement d, the empirical measure concentrates on the Boltzmann solution for t ∈ [0, T₀].

tests.name: equilibrium
tests.statement: At the Maxwellian equilibrium on the unit torus in dimension d ≥ 2 (μ_ε → ∞) the hypotheses hold with f = M by §9.4 and §9.6.

tests.name: poisson_variance
tests.statement: ε = 0, t = 0: Var(π(h)) = μ^{−1} ∫ f⁰ h².

tests.name: needs_F2
tests.statement: If F_2 → 2 f ⊗ f the variance tends to (∫ f h)² > 0.

tests.name: dimension_one
tests.statement: d = 1: μ_ε = 1; on the unit circle with f⁰ = M, Z_ε → e, P(N = 1) → e^{−1}, and for h = 1, δ = 1/2, P(|π^ε_t(1) − 1| ≥ 1/2) → 1 − e^{−1} ≈ 0.63212, not 0.
